review_scope: Independent source, sample-membership, execution-evidence and cost-projection review for the CPU-only R2 feature profile

independent_checks.detail: The admission hashes bind the profile module, feature module, entrypoint and historical recipe bytes. The emitted profile result repeats the recipe SHA and all feature/source hashes. The current recipe file can advance to a deferred status without changing the bytes preserved in PROFILE_RECIPE_R2.json.

independent_checks.check: Selected fit membership and evaluation exclusion
independent_checks.detail: Independently checked all eight sampled row groups in each fold against the frozen subset and split SHA. F0 samples are [6,279,534,757,1028,1268,1592,1863] and all belong to its 118 selected fit-valid groups, disjoint from 468 evaluation groups. F1 samples are [16,203,446,825,1105,1384,1651,1833] and all belong to its 172 selected fit-valid groups, disjoint from 457 evaluation groups. The recipe evaluation order matches both split manifests.

The frozen profile opens valid.parquet and calls SequenceFile.read with targets=false and mask=false for normalizer samples and feature streams. It reads raw 112-wide features only, never opens train.parquet as a ParquetFile, and computes no prediction, loss or score. Split/subset validation uses manifests and feature-only connectivity/index metadata.

For each fold, verified the one-pass projection as the fastest of eight observed six-stream times multiplied by complete fit-plus-evaluation sequence passes: F0 4.571106707 s × 1,704 = 7,789.165829 s; F1 4.723362395 s × 1,700 = 8,029.716071 s. The sum is 15,818.881900 s, which exceeds the unchanged 9,000 s inclusive ceiling by 6,818.881900 s (75.8%). The three-epoch recompute estimate independently sums to 38,860.936594 s.

The immutable execution result and raw /usr/bin/time log agree on 92.16 seconds wall time, 386,316 KiB maximum RSS, zero swaps and exit code 0. The admitted one-CPU scope was capped at 800,000,000 bytes; the controller observed a 506,081,280-byte cgroup peak while the transient scope was live and recorded why that peak is not available after exit.

findings.budget_gate: The unchanged 12-fit panel is deferred intact under the frozen 9,000-second ceiling. The measured implementation's optimistic one-pass feature projection alone is above budget, before fitting normalizers over all members, train/evaluation reads, parent prediction caches, GPU updates, exports, checkpoints, sidecars, grading or native delivery.
findings.quality: No fitted endpoint or prediction was produced. This is cost evidence, not a negative online-learning result and not a grader result.

limitations: The observed timing is a one-CPU NumPy profile using eight complete fit-valid sequences per fold from valid.parquet. It is an empirical optimistic projection from each fold's fastest sample, not a mathematical lower bound on every future implementation or machine state.

The projection extrapolates identical per-sequence feature work to train and evaluation groups; it omits source-specific read costs and all fit, parent-cache, export and grading costs. The full train parquet reader and train-footer memory were not measured in R2; R1's separate 800 MB OOM remains an infrastructure failure, not scientific evidence.

An explicitly revised and measured optimized feature implementation could change the cost estimate. This receipt does not authorize a new recipe or a fit; any reopening remains under root-owned admission and the unchanged panel/cost policy.
decision: Independent review supports deferring the current complete panel for cost only. Preserve the 12-fit design and all prior records; make no quality inference.
